bull.t: Recurring subscription and premium access growth
bull.b: Subscription revenue's larger mix and premium retention provide more predictable monetization than purely transactional licensing. This recurring base can support customer lifetime value and revenue resilience, while premium and Unsplash+ growth indicate continued demand for differentiated access.

Editorial growth and sharply higher custom-content activity broaden Getty's revenue sources beyond standard image licensing. Stronger news, archive, and tailored-content demand can deepen enterprise relationships and improve the platform's ability to monetize specialized content.

C2PA verification, natural-language search, AI editing, and expanded distribution partnerships strengthen the product proposition. These initiatives can improve discovery, trust, workflow integration, and reach, helping Getty defend relevance as content creation and licensing evolve.

bear.t: NYSE delisting and reduced market access
bear.b: NYSE delisting and the move to OTC Pink reduce investor access and may weaken trading liquidity or quoting continuity. Even if management says underlying operations are unaffected, this structural market-access change can complicate financing, stakeholder engagement, and capital allocation.

Free cash flow of negative $122.6 million after a $110.9 million litigation payment demonstrates a major cash outflow shock, while adjusted FCF was still negative $4.5 million. This limits internally funded investment and increases reliance on financing while the judgment is unresolved.

Debt of about $2.1 billion, high-cost notes, only $51.6 million cash, and $80.4 million quarterly cash interest leave limited financial flexibility. Elevated servicing costs can absorb operating resources and constrain investment, refinancing options, and the company's ability to withstand further pressure.
